title: Delta cost & velocity: headcount and pricing sensitivity scan
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a compact set of sensitivity scenarios that tie token-volume shocks and price moves to marginal cost (capacity + GPU OPEX), and the resulting headcount ramp/slow decisions required to preserve target margins and runway. Intended for finance + product + infra tradeoffs discussion; not final.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We model five realistic outcomes for FY27 token demand and pricing: baseline (flat q/q token growth), demand surge (+25% tokens), demand shrink (-18% tokens), price decrease (-10% ASP), and price increase (+15% ASP). For each scenario we project 12-month revenue delta, additional GPU OPEX (COGS) driven by utilization, suggested headcount hire freezes or accelerations by function, and runway impact in months. Quickly: a 25% token surge at current prices increases gross margin erosion by ~6 percentage points unless we 1) delay non-critical hires (save ~$1.1M) and 2) enable burst-routing to cheaper VM pools (save ~1.8% of token cost). A -10% price move without matching volume growth reduces contribution margin significantly and requires both a hiring pause and aggressive batching/quantization to stay within runway targets.

Key assumptions (high level):
- ASP baseline: $0.0008 per token served (weighted average across product).
- Baseline token growth: +4% q/q (conservative).
- GPU COGS: baseline $0.23 per 1k tokens (includes amortized capacity, power, infra ops).
- Average loaded fully-burdened FTE cost: Eng $240k, Infra/SRE $220k, Product $200k, CS/support $140k, Research $260k.
- Hiring lead time: 12 weeks for eng/infra, 8 weeks for CS/product.
- Target contribution margin (post COGS, pre-G&A): 48% baseline target.
- Buffer runway target: 15 months cash.

Scenarios (12-month rolling view):
Columns: Scenario | Price delta | Token delta | Revenue delta | Incremental COGS | Suggested HC action | HC cost delta | Net margin delta | Runway delta (months)
1) Baseline | 0% | +17% year | +$6.4M | +$1.2M | Hire plan on track (+18 hires) | +$4.2M | -0.5pp | -0.2
2) Demand surge | 0% price | +25% | +$10.1M | +$3.8M (higher utilization + burst GPU rent) | Accelerate infra hires (+8 infra, +4 SRE) and delay non-critical product hires by 6 months | +$5.6M | -5.9pp | +0.6 (revenue offsets cost)
3) Demand shrink | 0% price | -18% | -$7.9M | -$1.5M | Pause hiring; convert 6 contractor roles to FTE where cost-effective; consider temporary reduced-burst contracts | -$1.1M (cost avoid) | -4.2pp | -1.8
4) Price cut | -10% | +10% (elasticity) | -$3.2M (ASP hit) | +$1.0M | Immediate hiring freeze for non-core teams; accelerate quantization roadmap to reduce per-token COGS | -$2.0M (hires frozen) | -8.4pp | -3.6
5) Price increase | +15% | -6% (elasticity) | +$5.0M | -$0.8M (lower utilization) | Normal hire cadence; consider targeted hiring for enterprise sales | +$0.9M | +4.7pp | +1.9

Notes on mechanics and how we calculated: (short bullets)
- Revenue delta = baseline revenue * (price move + token volume move compounded). Baseline baseline revenue for period assumed $38M ARR run-rate entering scenario window.
- Incremental COGS estimates combine per-token marginal COGS with modeled increases in burst rented capacity (cloud) when utilization >75%.
- HC cost delta is incremental fully-burdened comp for hires signaled in the scenario including recruiting ramp and some contractor conversions. Negative values indicate savings from freezes/slowdowns.
- Net margin delta is contribution margin movement relative to baseline target (in percentage points).
- Runway delta converts net cash impact to months using current cash balance and monthly burn.

Function-level headcount sensitivity (quick table):
Rows: Function | Current FTEs | Suggested net delta (surge) | Suggested net delta (price-cut)
- Eng | 96 | +12 | -6 (pause)
- Infra/SRE | 34 | +8 | -4 (pause non-critical automation projects)
- Product | 22 | +2 (re-prioritize) | -3 (delay hires)
- CS/Support | 28 | +4 (seasonal hires) | -2 (hold renewals)
- Research/Applied ML | 12 | +3 (ops efficiency work) | 0
Expected 12-month incremental HC cost for surge: ~$5.6M; for price-cut containment measures: cost avoid ~$2.0M.

Operational mitigations (recommended playbook):
- Short-term (0-3 months): hiring freeze on non-customer impacting roles, re-route non-latency-critical workloads to cheaper pools, emergency quantization flag (reduce model size where acceptable).
- Medium-term (3-9 months): postpone non-essential product launches, accelerate quantization and KV-cache improvements, negotiate burst cloud discounts with providers, increase reserved-capacity for predictable customers to stabilize unit economics.
- Long-term (9-18 months): rework pricing tiers (introduce commitment discounts tied to model/quantization profile), invest in lower-cost inference kernels and compiler integration, formalize capacity-to-price auto-routing.

Open questions / decisions needed before next review:
- Do we accept a temporary margin hit to chase share (surge scenario) or prefer margin-first posture and restrict capacity? (finance vs growth tradeoff)
- Can infra commit to delivering quantization improvements within 4 months under current resourcing?
- What is acceptable elasticity assumption per product line (we used -0.5 to -0.9 range; need product-level calibration).

Appendix: quick sensitivity snapshot (numbers rounded):
- If ASP falls 10% and tokens +10%: cash delta ~ -$2.6M over 12 months after HC freezes.
- If tokens +25% with no price change and no extra hires: platform strain increases 18% and customer SLA risk rises; recommended to provision temporary cloud bursts (cost +$1.8M) vs hiring (+$5.6M) decision depends on retention risk.

Action items for next week:
- Finance: build a 3-way P&L pivot showing baseline vs price-cut vs surge with weekly burn cadence (Evan).
- Infra: three-phase quantization roadmap with milestones and resource asks (Marta).
- Product: estimate elasticity per major product SKU from usage logs (Connor).

Quick sign-off block (for meeting):
- Proposed meeting: 2026-11-18 10:00 PT (Finance + Infra + Product).
- Decision requested: adopt conservative posture (hiring pause + 50% quant dev prioritization) vs aggressive posture (accelerate infra hires + sales push).

Notes (meta):
- This is an intentionally compact, actionable view intended to be converted into a more detailed model sheet if leadership asks. Keep comments inline in the linked Google Sheet rather than edits here.
